title: LCF-24: MRF Search and Rescue Efforts
description: U.S. Marines with Maritime Raid Force, Littoral Combat Force-24, conduct a search and rescue in La Guaira, Venezuela, June 26, through 30, 2026. At the direction of U.S. Southern Command assigned U.S. military forces are supporting Department of State-led U.S. disaster assistance to the people of Venezuela in the aftermath of the June 24, 2026, earthquakes. (U.S. Marine Corps video)
keywords: 24th MEU, MRF, usmcnews, LCF-24, VenEarthquake, JTFWHEM

transcript.text: Prior to the earthquakes in Venezuela ,
we were assigned to other tasking
inside of the US SOCOM area of
responsibility , primarily supporting ,
uh , quick reaction force contingencies ,
uh , within the AO . Our primary
focus as the maritime raid force during
that period of time was mostly on
maritime interception operations . We
were training and really sustaining our
capability to conduct MEO
operations , um , in support of the uh
combatant commander .
So when the earthquakes first happened ,
We found out about it first through our
chain of command , uh , and you know ,
understood very quickly that the
situation was very bad , that it was a
very devastating event for the
Venezuelan people . There were two
places that were primarily stated that
were affected by the earthquake . One

The situation developed rather quickly .
We knew relatively early on the best
way that the maritime raid force could
contribute was going to be through
search and rescue . Because of that ,
we knew that the clock was ticking and
we had to get there as soon as possible ,
so it really compressed the amount of
time that we had to plan and to prepare
so we got ourselves ready as quickly as
we could to get on the ground and see
what we could do to help . When we
arrived on the deck in LaGuardia , the
level of welcome that we received
cannot be understated . I have never
felt more welcomed by people in my
entire career and and really in my life .
We inserted in helicopters on an
abandoned golf course in in the heart

most of the destruction was , and as we
walked from that . Point to where we
would be staying for the next several
days . There were people , refugees ,
Venezuelan people rising to their feet ,
you know , saying USA , thank you ,
thank you Marines , just absolutely
open arms as we arrived . The people
that we were helping while we were in
LaGuardia , if I were to put myself in
their shoes , it's , it would be , it's ,
it would be very difficult to truly do
that . The level of destruction . Um ,
and the , the level of human suffering ,
I mean , it's , it truly is hard to
describe unless you were actually there
and you could see it for yourself .
What was out on social media , what was
out on the news with the pictures and
the videos , it truly just does not do
it justice . You had to be there . You
had to see these people , the pain that
they were going through , and just the
sheer level of destruction . Uh ,

could feel the pain from the people
that were there . It really just truly
brought out the best in every single
one of us , every single one of us just
wanted to do whatever we possibly could
to try to help these people .
So going through we had um we had
different signs of life going into the
uh the destruction and everything and
we would dig tunnels to try to get to
these uh to get to these people that
were buried in the rubble and if it

signs of life , people inside and

definitely strategic to say the least .
What's the tunnel look like ? What's
the debris ? What's the structure that
I'm , I'm going to be crawling into and
chipping away at ? Definitely played a
factor in what was going on and
extremely hot in those tunnels too , so
the heat alone , but it was kind of as

can we relay up there's there's a lot

the outside .
What I've learned from this is that the
Venezuelan people are very strong
people that can endure a lot , uh , but
they don't have to endure it alone .
That they have the United States Marine
Corps , the United States of America
writ large , and , and really the

they can lean on to help them through
this situation , um , and it was really
just an absolute honor and a pleasure
to , to have the opportunity to have
been there uh and to have helped those
people in any way that we could .
